title: 321. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Complementary and Supplementary Angles
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify pairs of angles that are complementary.
questions.question: Which pair of angles is complementary?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles are two angles whose measures add to \(90^\circ\). For option A, \(35^\circ + 55^\circ = 90^\circ\), so this pair is complementary. For option B, \(35^\circ + 65^\circ = 100^\circ\), which is not \(90^\circ\). Therefore, the correct pair is \(35^\circ\) and \(55^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall that complementary angles have a sum of \(90^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the defining property of supplementary angles.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes supplementary angles?

options.label: A
options.text: Two angles are supplementary if their measures add to \(180^\circ\).

options.label: B
options.text: Two angles are supplementary if their measures add to \(90^\circ\).

questions.explanation: Supplementary angles are defined as two angles whose measures have a sum of \(180^\circ\). The statement that their measures add to \(90^\circ\) describes complementary angles instead. Therefore, the correct description is that their measures add to \(180^\circ\).
questions.hint: Distinguish carefully between sums of \(90^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the measure of the complement of a given angle.
questions.question: An angle measures \(28^\circ\). What is the measure of its complement?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to \(90^\circ\). Therefore, the complement of \(28^\circ\) is \(90^\circ - 28^\circ = 62^\circ\). The value \(152^\circ\) comes from subtracting from \(180^\circ\), which finds a supplement, not a complement.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the measure of the supplement of a given angle.
questions.question: An angle measures \(73^\circ\). What is the measure of its supplement?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to \(180^\circ\). Thus, the supplement of \(73^\circ\) is \(180^\circ - 73^\circ = 107^\circ\). The value \(17^\circ\) is the complement of \(73^\circ\), not its supplement.

questions.learningObjective: Determine angle measures from a ratio when the angles are complementary.
questions.question: Two complementary angles are in the ratio \(2:3\). What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Let the two angles be \(2k\) and \(3k\). Since they are complementary, \(2k + 3k = 90^\circ\). This gives \(5k = 90^\circ\), so \(k = 18^\circ\). The larger angle is \(3k = 3 \times 18^\circ = 54^\circ\). Therefore, the larger angle measures \(54^\circ\).
questions.hint: Represent the angles as \(2k\) and \(3k\), then use the fact that their sum is \(90^\circ\).

questions.concept: Supplementary Angles with a Given Difference
questions.learningObjective: Determine angle measures from a difference condition when the angles are supplementary.
questions.question: Two supplementary angles differ by \(40^\circ\). What is the measure of the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Let the larger angle be \(x\) and the smaller angle be \(y\). Since the angles are supplementary, \(x + y = 180^\circ\). Since they differ by \(40^\circ\), \(x - y = 40^\circ\). Adding the two equations gives \(2x = 220^\circ\), so \(x = 110^\circ\). Therefore, the larger angle measures \(110^\circ\).
questions.hint: Set up two equations using the sum \(180^\circ\) and the given difference.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for an angle given a relationship between the angle and its complement.
questions.question: An angle is \(20^\circ\) more than its complement. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angle be \(x\). Its complement is \(90^\circ - x\). The condition says \(x = (90^\circ - x) + 20^\circ\). Simplifying gives \(x = 110^\circ - x\), so \(2x = 110^\circ\) and \(x = 55^\circ\). Therefore, the angle measures \(55^\circ\).
questions.hint: Write the complement as \(90^\circ - x\), then translate the phrase “more than” into an equation.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for an angle given a relationship between the angle and its supplement.
questions.question: An angle is twice its supplement. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angle be \(x\). Its supplement is \(180^\circ - x\). The condition says \(x = 2(180^\circ - x)\). Expanding gives \(x = 360^\circ - 2x\), so \(3x = 360^\circ\) and \(x = 120^\circ\). Therefore, the angle measures \(120^\circ\).
questions.hint: Write the supplement as \(180^\circ - x\), then set the angle equal to twice that expression.

questions.learningObjective: Use algebra to find an unknown in complementary angles.
questions.question: The measures of two complementary angles are \(x+10\) and \(2x-4\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Since the angles are complementary, their measures add to \(90^\circ\). Thus, \((x+10) + (2x-4) = 90\). Combining like terms gives \(3x + 6 = 90\). Subtracting \(6\) from both sides gives \(3x = 84\), so \(x = 28\). Therefore, the value of \(x\) is \(28\).
questions.hint: Set the sum of the two expressions equal to \(90^\circ\), then solve the resulting linear equation.

questions.concept: Angle Related to Twice Its Complement
questions.learningObjective: Solve a multi-step relationship involving an angle and twice its complement.
questions.question: An angle measures \(15^\circ\) more than twice its complement. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angle be \(x\). Its complement is \(90^\circ - x\). The condition says \(x = 2(90^\circ - x) + 15^\circ\). Expanding gives \(x = 180^\circ - 2x + 15^\circ\), so \(x = 195^\circ - 2x\). Adding \(2x\) to both sides gives \(3x = 195^\circ\), so \(x = 65^\circ\). Therefore, the angle measures \(65^\circ\).
questions.hint: Express the complement as \(90^\circ - x\), then translate “twice its complement plus \(15^\circ\)” into an equation.
